title: Place the proxy before assigning it authority
description: Choose who the proxy represents, what protocol layer it understands, where TLS ends, and which hop may assert client identity. The path updates to show what the proxy can actually route, inspect, and trust.

directions.label: Forward proxy
directions.detail: Chosen for clients; controls or observes their outbound destinations.
directions.purpose: The proxy represents clients to destination services and enforces outbound policy.

directions.label: Reverse proxy
directions.detail: Chosen by the service owner; accepts traffic before internal backends.
directions.purpose: The proxy represents the service, admits requests, and selects an internal destination.

layers.label: Layer 4
layers.detail: Routes transport connections without parsing the application request.
layers.inspection: Source and destination addresses, ports, connection state, and byte counts
layers.routing: IP address, port, transport metadata, or connection hash
layers.loadSignal: Open connections are a useful signal only when connection cost tracks backend work.

layers.label: Layer 7
layers.detail: Parses HTTP or another application protocol for request-aware policy.
layers.inspection: Host, path, method, headers, cookies, status, and request timing
layers.routing: Host, path, method, header, cookie, or authenticated request context
layers.loadSignal: Active requests and observed response behavior can be more useful than connection count.

tlsModes.label: TLS pass-through
tlsModes.detail: The proxy forwards encrypted bytes; the destination owns the certificate and plaintext.

tlsModes.label: Terminate at proxy
tlsModes.detail: The proxy decrypts requests and sends plaintext on the controlled upstream network.

tlsModes.label: Terminate and re-encrypt
tlsModes.detail: The proxy applies L7 policy, then creates and verifies a separate upstream TLS connection.

identityPolicies.label: Trust any inbound forwarding header
identityPolicies.detail: The application accepts the first X-Forwarded-For or identity value it receives.

identityPolicies.label: Normalize at the trusted edge
identityPolicies.detail: The edge removes untrusted values and writes one canonical client identity field.
identityPolicies.result: Only the known edge may assert forwarding identity

identityPolicies.label: Authenticated proxy hop
identityPolicies.detail: The receiver accepts a signed header or PROXY protocol only from an authenticated or allowlisted peer.
identityPolicies.result: Transport peer and metadata authority are checked together
